walkthroughs.body_html:
Readers, Writers and Texts — a core area of English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Readers, Writers and Texts brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Readers, Writers and Texts.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who coined the term unreliable narrator in 1961?
options: Wayne Booth
Northrop Frye
F R Leavis
Mikhail Bakhtin

mcqs.q: Which Marquez novel exemplifies magic realism?
options: Love in the Time of Cholera
One Hundred Years of Solitude
The Autumn of the Patriarch
Chronicle of a Death Foretold
Pathetic fallacy is when an argument in a story is weak or sad.
Pathetic fallacy is when characters cry over silly things.
Attributing human emotions or qualities to nature or inanimate objects to reflect a character's feelings or scene's mood (e.g. angry storms during conflict).
Romantic poets believed nature was full of fairies and elves.

mcqs.q: What did Romantic poets value in nature?
options: Romantic poets believed nature was full of fairies and elves.
Nature as a source of spiritual insight and emotional truth, accessed through imagination — not picturesque scenery for its own sake.
Modernism is literature about modern technology like phones.
Romantic poets just liked to write about pretty landscapes.
Modernism just means literature written in modern times.
Experimentation with form (fragmentation, stream of consciousness), focus on subjective interior experience, scepticism toward traditional narrative and absolute truth.
Pathetic fallacy is when characters cry over silly things.
Modernism is literature about modern technology like phones.
